newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU likely to tell ASEAN not time to talk to Burma.
newsitem.headline: EU likely to tell ASEAN not time to talk to Burma.

text.p: European Union foreign ministers are expected to tell ASEAN on Thursday that Burma's membership of the Asian trading bloc does not mean the EU is ready to let Rangoon into joint EU-Asian talks.
EU sources said the ministers, meeting in Luxembourg, would discuss the situation in Burma, particularly concerning what is seen as a lack of improvement in respect for human rights.
ASEAN, the Association of South East Asian Nations, will formally embrace Burma as a member at its next ministerial meeting in Malaysia on July 24-25.

But the EU ministers are expected to tell the group that this does not mean the EU will allow Burma to participate in ASEM, the main EU-Asia discussion forum, or to begin talks on joining other ASEAN members in a cooperation pact with the EU.
The EU, reacting to accusations of human rights abuse by the Rangoon military government, has cut off high-level contacts with Burma and withdrawn various trading privileges.
The sources said some EU countries may raise the possibility of further sanctions at Thursday's meeting, but that a decision on it was likely to be put off to a further meeting.
